tested_scope.model: 576 finite traces = 6 protocols x 96 valid history/recovery/credential/prior-effect/transport states. Per protocol: 32 legitimately-old traces with no newer external witness plus 64 rolled-back-after-g2 traces split evenly by whether a newer external witness survives.
tested_scope.external_newer_witness: For rolled-back histories only, either a signed/monotonic g2 witness survives outside the rollback domains or no such newer witness is available. Legitimately-old worlds have no g2 witness by construction.
tested_scope.unsafe_definition: Unsafe means accepting a g1-generation action after g2 has existed, accepting a stale-incarnation action after name rebind, or applying the same semantic effect more than once after effect-history loss/response loss.
tested_scope.excluded: Byzantine signature forgery, probabilistic storage-retention claims, generic availability of any non-rollbackable external domain, arbitrary distributed consensus, and Part128 repository-incarnation write-time fencing.

protocols.client_carried_signed_certificate: Use a surviving client-carried signed g2 certificate as a freshness witness when one exists; otherwise trust the currently visible g1 authority and keep no permanent effect ledger.
protocols.repository_hash_chain_current_only: Validate current repository hash-chain/commit identity only; no remembered newer head exists outside the rollbackable repository. Reject stale rebind credentials when current incarnation mismatches, but keep no permanent effect ledger.
protocols.sink_incarnation_binding: Validate current sink incarnation and reject stale credentials after same-name rebind; keep no non-rollbackable generation/effect-history floor.
protocols.dual_repository_sink_current_witnesses: Require current repository and current sink witnesses to agree, but both witnesses may be restored together to the same old view and no third monotonic floor is retained.
protocols.external_nonrollbackable_anchor_control: Positive control: a recovery domain outside both rollback domains permanently records the highest generation/incarnation plus effect IDs and rejects g1 once g2 has existed.
protocols.fail_closed_on_recovery_uncertainty: Safety-only control: refuse all actions after complete repository+sink recovery uncertainty until an equivalent non-rollbackable floor/history is re-established.

dual_repository_sink_current_witnesses.common_mode_current_after_recovery: accepts old mutually-consistent view and cannot prove g2 never existed

indistinguishability_witness.construction: For every recovery/credential/prior-effect/transport tuple with no surviving newer external witness, pair a legitimately-old g1 history with a history in which g2 existed and both repository authority plus sink-local state were restored/rebound to the same visible g1 state. Current repository identity, current sink identity/state, and absence of a newer client witness are identical by construction.
indistinguishability_witness.strict_pair_conditions: current-after-recovery credential, no prior same effect, and either clean or rate-limit-before-apply/later-retry transport, across both recovery modes. In the legitimately-old member, accepting the g1 effect is safe/useful under the modeled contract; in the rolled-back member, the same acceptance is stale-generation unsafe.
indistinguishability_witness.consequence: Any deterministic protocol whose entire evidence is confined to the jointly rollbackable repository+sink current views and an absent newer client witness must make the same decision in each pair. Accepting violates rollback safety; rejecting sacrifices useful progress in the legitimately-old member. Randomization cannot provide zero-error safety plus guaranteed usefulness on two observationally identical states.
indistinguishability_witness.minimal_escape: At least one observation must come from a recovery domain whose monotonic fact survives the common-mode rollback (for example a durable highest-generation/effect-history anchor or an equivalently persistent client witness). If that witness is absent, fail-closed refusal is safe but does not establish useful-outcome parity.

diagnostic_slices.ambiguous_prior_effect_after_rollback_wi: The client-certificate protocol was 16/16 unsafe; current-only repository/sink/dual protocols were 12/16 unsafe and rejected only the 4 stale-rebind-credential cases. Lost effect history is therefore an independent duplicate-risk dimension even when incarnation binding catches name reuse.
diagnostic_slices.same_name_rebind_stale_credential_withou: Repository-current, sink-incarnation and dual-current protocols rejected 8/8; client-certificate-only accepted 8/8 unsafely. Incarnation binding solves this narrow stale-name case but not common-mode generation rollback with a refreshed credential.
diagnostic_slices.rate_limit_semantics: Rate-limit-before-apply causes no effect and no same-run retry. The later retry is a later invocation. Results therefore do not rely on waiting, polling, hosted compute or quota-bearing execution.

observed: Across the 32 paired no-newer-witness observations, repository-current, sink-current and dual-current evidence can be identical in a legitimately-old g1 world and a rolled-back-after-g2 world.
Four strict pairs require opposite decisions for safe useful behavior: accept in the legitimately-old member, reject in the rolled-back member.

A surviving newer client certificate distinguishes all 32 rolled-back traces modeled for the client-certificate protocol, but the certificate is itself a witness outside the rolled-back repository+sink domains.
The external non-rollbackable anchor positive control produced 0/96 unsafe traces; fail-closed refusal also produced 0/96 unsafe traces but accepted none.
observation_vs_inference.inference: Within this finite model, no protocol restricted to two simultaneously rollbackable current-state domains can provide both zero-error rollback safety and useful progress for the strict indistinguishable pairs. A client-carried signed certificate helps only if some durable client state survives the rollback; that surviving state is functionally the required third non-rollbackable recovery domain. Repository hash identity or dual current witnesses are not sufficient when the authority that defines their freshness can itself be restored to an old self-consistent view.

conditional_safe_mechanisms: one non-rollbackable monotonic generation/incarnation/effect-history recovery domain
surviving client-held newer signed witness treated as that recovery domain
fail-closed refusal until such a witness is re-established
phase1_assessment.residual_richer_mode_protected_manual_ex: none in this bounded self-local model; generic recovery after all available freshness domains roll back remains unresolved
phase1_assessment.quota_zero_rule: Only lightweight repository transport and local finite reasoning were used; no hosted runner, Codespaces, artifact/LFS/package quota, external coordinator, paid credit, or manual user execution is part of the tested mechanism.

unresolved_children: Find a zero-cost Chat-native recovery domain whose monotonic freshness/effect-history fact is independent of repository+sink common-mode rollback; absence of such a primitive remains unresolved rather than proving root impossibility.

Determine whether immutable Git object identity plus a separately retained SHA can survive force-push, repository delete/recreate, unreachable-object collection and same-name reuse strongly enough to count as a generic recovery witness without importing paid/hosted coordination.
Part128 repository-incarnation write-time fencing remains unresolved and must not be promoted to generic acceptance by this result.
continuation: Part132: execute one bounded Git-object/retained-SHA recovery-witness leaf. Hold Parts128-131 fixed. Test whether immutable commit/blob identity plus a separately retained SHA can act as the needed zero-cost non-rollbackable freshness witness across branch force-rewind, repository delete/recreate, same-name reuse, unreachable-object retention/garbage-collection uncertainty, response loss, rate-limit interruption and later retry. Separate (a) content-address authenticity, (b) discoverability/reachability, and (c) freshness/anti-rollback. If the SHA itself must survive in another durable domain, count that domain explicitly rather than treating the hash as self-remembering. Use only own clean state and public sources, no hosted compute/coordinator/finite quota/manual execution; absence of a generic guarantee is an unresolved child, not closure.
